introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ. Moses seals the covenant with the blood of sacrifice. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Christ, our high priest, entered the sanctuary with his own blood. In the Gospel, Jesus gives his disciples his Body and Blood at the Last Supper. In many places, a procession with the Blessed Sacrament follows Mass. Let us adore Christ, truly present among us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ gives us his Body and Blood as our food. Let us bring our prayers to the Father with grateful hearts.
intentions: For the Church: that she may grow in love for the Eucharist and draw from it her strength for mission. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests: that they may celebrate the Eucharist with faith and lead God's people to adore Christ present in it. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are hungry for bread or for meaning: that Christians may share both with them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who cannot receive Communion, and those who have drifted from the Mass: that Christ may draw them to his table. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may receive the Body of Christ worthily and become what we receive. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus Christ, you gave us your Body and Blood in the new covenant. Help us to adore you in this sacrament and to serve you in our brothers and sisters. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: The blood of the covenant
reflection.body:
At Sinai, Moses reads the book of the covenant to the people, and they answer, "We will do all that the LORD has said, and be obedient." Then he takes the blood of the sacrifice and sprinkles it on them, saying, "Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which the LORD has made with you." Blood meant life. God and his people were bound together in one life.

At the Last Supper, Jesus takes up those very words. He takes bread and says, "Take, eat. This is my body." He takes the cup and says, "This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many." The old covenant was sealed with the blood of animals; the new covenant is sealed with the blood of the Son of God.

The Letter to the Hebrews explains what this means. Christ entered the sanctuary not "through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood," once for all, "having obtained eternal redemption." And it asks: "how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?"

The psalm gives us our response: "I will take the cup of salvation, and call on the LORD's name." Every Mass makes this covenant present. Christ does not only remember us; he gives himself to us as food.

If there is a Corpus Christi procession today, take part in it, carrying Christ through the streets where we live and work. This week, spend a few minutes before the tabernacle, and thank the Lord who chose to stay with us under the signs of bread and wine.
